newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Scientists back EU meat hormone ban.
newsitem.headline: Scientists back EU meat hormone ban.

text.p: A European Union ban on imports of hormone-treated beef from the United States is based on sound science, leading scientists said on Wednesday.

The scientists, participating in a European Parliament symposium on the use of growth hormones in meat production, criticised a recent preliminary ruling against the ban by the World Trade Organisation.
The EU, which is studying the confidential report by a WTO disputes panel, is being pressed by France and other EU countries to contest the ruling.
"We believe the scientific evidence is overwhelming," Samuel Epstein, Professor of Environmental and Occupational Medicine at the University of Illinois, told a news conference.

Epstein, who is also Chairman of the Chicago-based Cancer Prevention Coalition, said that lifelong exposure to residues of natural and synthetic growth hormones in meat poses significant risk of breast cancer as well as feminising traits.
American attempts to present the hormonal dispute as between consumers and scientists were unfounded, he said.
"Consumerism is backed by sound science against ignorance, bias and conflicts of interest," Epstein said.
He rejected a recent claim by the U.S. Department of Agriculture that there was no sign of excessive drug levels in meat products.
Not one of the 130 million livestock slaughtered in 1993 had been tested for cancer-causing and gene-damaging estradiol, or any related sex hormone, he said.
"We have no idea of hormonal levels in U.S. meat," he said.
Professor Georg Liehr, of the University of Texas Department of Pharmacology and Toxicology, said the WTO report was scientifically flawed.

"The WTO report ...is not supported by science," he said, adding that it was based on a 1988 report by the U.N. Food and Agriculture Organisation and the World Health Organisation using data from the 1970s.
Epstein added that the WTO panel was advised mainly by industry consultants, regulatory officials and veterinary scientists rather than independent experts in preventive medicine and public health.
Professor Manfred Metzler of Germany's University of Karlsruhe, agreed that European consumers must be protected against health dangers from hormones.
"Natural and synthetic hormones cause a cancer risk," he said, adding they were used for economic profit and should be banned.
